transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (AstraGrid Head of Platform), Liam (FinOps), Hannah (SRE), Marcus (PM)

Summary: quick health check and decision sync focused on runway, cost commitments, and pilot scope. Primary ask from AstraGrid: get predictable latency under 120ms p50 for their chat surface while getting cost per active session down ~18% vs current vendor.

Topics: usage trends, cost breakdown, latency SLOs, private/VPC pilot scope, security/compliance questions, pilot acceptance criteria, next steps and owners

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): all right, thanks everyone for joining. quick agenda — run through usage & cost signals, then diego will walk through the dedicated pool perf plan, then open q&a and decide pilot commitments. sound good?
[00:12] Priya (AstraGrid): yep, that's perfect. we're short on time today so if we can focus on the SLOs and the financial tradeoffs that would be great.
[00:22] Diego (Redwood): cool. i'll start with a quick snapshot. based on the telemetry you already shared, your p50 token latency on current vendor is ~180ms for the chat flow at 1k concurrent sessions. with Redwood Dedicated we expect to be closer to 90-120ms depending on batching and KV-cache warm state, so that meets your 120ms p50 ask in steady state. caveat — burst cold starts will be higher unless we provision some minimum pool.
[00:45] Hannah (AstraGrid): what do you mean by "minimum pool"? are we talking reserved GPUs or a warm standby? our infra team is sensitive to ops overhead.
[00:53] Diego (Redwood): reserved GPUs — you can set a min pool size, say 2 GPUs kept hot for the fastest latency. autoscale will add nodes for throughput. that's the Dedicated model. hosted would be more elastic but less predictable latency during spikes.
[01:14] Liam (AstraGrid): cost question — if we reserve 2 GPUs vs using hosted on-demand, what's ballpark impact for monthly spend? we need numbers to compare to current contract.
[01:24] Maya (Redwood): we'll send a pricing scenarios sheet after the call — brief answer: reserved shows savings when sustained utilization > 40% because of amortized baseline. with your traffic patterns we think a committed 1yr plan with minimal burst capacity could reduce unit costs ~15-25%. we'll model a few mixes.
[01:40] Marcus (AstraGrid): are there any extra licensing or enterprise fees for private deployment / VPC? we have compliance rules that push us to keep data inside our VPC if possible.
[01:49] Maya (Redwood): Private has a platform fee and typically support SLA add-ons. the core difference is control plane placement and direct VPC peering — we can bring a private control plane into your VPC or do site-to-site. also we support customer KMS for encryption at rest. i'll include the fees in the scenarios.
[02:10] Diego (Redwood): quick note on performance knobs — quantization helps cost but can slightly impact tail SLOs. prefix caching (we call KV cache) reduces token compute for assistant-style conversations, often giving a 20-40% per-token cost win for multi-turn. we can demo the effect in the pilot using a representative prompt corpus.
[02:32] Priya (AstraGrid): ok so pilot asks: 1) meet p50<120ms for chat; 2) show per-token cost delta with KV cache enabled; 3) security acceptance (SOC2, KMS integration) — is that right?
[02:44] Maya (Redwood): yes, that's exactly what we'll scope. plus a throughput stress run and a canary rollback plan for model rollouts.
[02:52] Hannah (AstraGrid): on security, our security team will want audit logs and retention policies, and proof of key isolation. do you integrate with HSM or just cloud KMS?
[03:03] Diego (Redwood): we support cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys for enterprise Private deployments. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM and we retain event-level logs per your retention policy in the pilot scope.
[03:16] Liam (AstraGrid): compliance also asks about data residency — our EU customers' data needs to stay in eu-west. can the pilot be region restricted?
[03:25] Maya (Redwood): absolutely. we can pin model serving and storage regions. for Dedicated we can guarantee region placement; for Private it's fully inside your infra.
[03:34] Marcus (AstraGrid): pricing — you mentioned committed 1yr. what if we want a 6-month pilot then decide on 12mo? we have procurement windows in mid-july.
[03:43] Maya (Redwood): flexible. typical path: short pilot (6-8 weeks) on dedicated test pool or hosted with reserved warm nodes, then if you sign 12mo we credit pilot usage toward committed spend. I'll put the exact credit terms in the pricing doc.
[03:58] Priya (AstraGrid): can we run a quick technical question — how do you handle KV cache invalidation when models roll forward? we've had incidents with stale context in the past.
[04:08] Diego (Redwood): good question. cache entries are keyed by model id + prompt prefix + user-session token; when you roll a model we atomically version the key namespace so old cache entries are ignored. we also expose a cache invalidation API for manual purge.
[04:27] Priya (AstraGrid): nice. that helps.
[04:34] Maya (Redwood): next, diego will outline the pilot test plan and timeline.
[04:39] Diego (Redwood): pilot plan (high level): week 0 - config and network setup (VPC peering / firewall rules), week 1 - baseline run with current traffic replay, week 2 - KV cache enabled + quantization profile, week 3 - 24h burst stress run and rollback exercise, week 4 - results & acceptance. we can compress if you want but that's the safe path.
[05:03] Hannah (AstraGrid): what's involved in the network setup from our side? we're on strict firewall egress rules.
[05:10] Diego (Redwood): you need to allow egress to the Redwood gateway IPs and open the specific ports for the control plane; if it's private deployment we install a control-plane appliance in your subnet so it's more of an install. we'll give a checklist.
[05:25] Liam (AstraGrid): about run costs during pilot — will we be billed for the whole reserved node even if utilization is low? we can't get hit with full committed until we sign.
[05:34] Maya (Redwood): in pilot we normally configure a smaller test pool and bill strictly for usage; committed billing kicks in once contractually agreed. the pricing doc will call out pilot billing terms.
[05:45] Priya (AstraGrid): competitors — we've run ModelServeX for a year. their latency is okay but cost is high and ops visibility is limited. we've also looked at BigCloud AI for a marketplace approach. how is Redwood different on observability?
[06:01] Diego (Redwood): in the Redwood console you get token-level cost breakdowns, trace hooks, per-model latency histograms, and prompt set-based quality alerts. plus rollouts have automatic fallback to cheaper model variants to keep availability. that visibility was a big focus in our build.
[06:20] Marcus (AstraGrid): are you able to map token cost back to a feature or route? our PMs need that for prioritization.
[06:28] Maya (Redwood): yes, per-route cost attribution is supported. we can tag requests to map to product features.
[06:35] Liam (AstraGrid): ok great. procurement question: what does the SOW look like for Dedicated? does Redwood require a minimum committed spend?
[06:44] Maya (Redwood): depends. for Dedicated we commonly do a monthly committed baseline; the number varies by GPU type and region. smaller customers can start with a lower committed band and scale. we'll propose three bands in the scenarios doc.
[06:58] Priya (AstraGrid): timeline constraints — we want pilot started by Jul 12 to hit our Q3 launch. can you support that?
[07:06] Diego (Redwood): yes, that's tight but doable. the VPC peering and security review are the usual blockers; if we get network details this week we can aim to be live by Jul 12.
[07:17] Priya (AstraGrid): i'll share the network and security contacts after the call.
[07:22] Maya (Redwood): i'll capture that as an action item. diego will also kick off the synthetic stress run this week.
[07:29] Diego (Redwood): i'll do a 24-hour burst test on the dedicated staging pool and share the resource utilization graphs. note: synthetic tests will be conservative vs real UR traffic patterns.
[07:40] Hannah (AstraGrid): for benchmarks we will also send real query traces (sanitized) so results are representative.
[07:48] Maya (Redwood): perfect — two artifacts we need: sanitized query set (10-15 representative prompts) and network/firewall checklist.
[07:55] Priya (AstraGrid): we'll do that by Monday.
[07:59] Liam (AstraGrid): one more question on billing — do you support cost-alloc tags so our FinOps can reconcile?
[08:06] Maya (Redwood): yes, we support tags at request and model level and provide exports compatible with common FinOps pipelines.
[08:13] Marcus (AstraGrid): any risk items we should be aware of?
[08:16] Diego (Redwood): a couple: 1) cold-start tail latency during infrequent huge bursts — mitigated by min pool; 2) quantization regressions on subjective prompts — we'll run small eval sets to qualify; 3) network egress constraints for the private control plane — that's on the customer's side to approve.
[08:36] Priya (AstraGrid): that aligns with our concerns.
[08:40] Maya (Redwood): okay time check — we've got about 45 minutes left; want to step through the acceptance criteria and signoff language.
[08:46] Priya (AstraGrid): yes please.
[08:49] Maya (Redwood): acceptance criteria (proposed): p50 latency < 120ms over 1M requests replayed, per-token cost reduction >=15% with KV cache on compared to current baseline, audit logs exported and KMS integration tested, and successful rollback exercise during stress run. if those pass, AstraGrid will move to procurement for committed capacity decision.
[09:15] Liam (AstraGrid): do you see any way to guarantee the cost reduction? we need some protection if numbers don't meet expectations after pilot.
[09:24] Maya (Redwood): we can include a performance SLA credit and pilot credit to lower risk; exact terms in contract.
[09:31] Priya (AstraGrid): procurement wants a default fallback: if Dedicated doesn't meet SLOs, we want an easy exit or conversion to hosted at prior rates.
[09:40] Maya (Redwood): reasonable — we'll draft language for pilot acceptance and fallback.
[09:46] Diego (Redwood): last technical note: when we enable quantization for cost savings we keep a small A/B on fidelity for critical flows to catch regressions.
[09:56] Marcus (AstraGrid): good.
[10:00] Maya (Redwood): ok, let's recap owners and timeline. next steps recap: redwood sends pricing scenarios & pilot SOW by Jul 3, customer sends sanitized queries and network details by Jul 6, security deep-dive week of Jul 13, target pilot start Jul 12, acceptance results week 4 of pilot.
[10:25] Priya (AstraGrid): sounds right.
[10:28] Liam (AstraGrid): agreed.
[10:30] Maya (Redwood): any final questions?
[10:32] Hannah (AstraGrid): none from me.
[10:33] Maya (Redwood): cool, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the doc pack and a calendar invite for the security deep-dive.
[10:40] Priya (AstraGrid): thanks.
[10:42] Maya (Redwood): bye all.

Meeting end.
